prerequisites: Having completed the basic training modules, common to the industrial branch and specific electrical technology.

learning_outcomes.text: Analyze the physical properties, charging process, and behavior of different types of batteries used in industrial and domestic systems.
Describe and analyze the operating principle of supercapacitors.
Describe and analyze the operating principle of electrochemical accumulators (batteries).
Differentiate the industrial application areas of electrical energy storage systems, as well as select the most suitable system in each case.
Understand the operating principle of fuel cells.

syllabus_topics: Review of conventional capacitors. Basic concepts.
Applications of SC: energy support, energy storage, hybrid automobiles, etc.
Equivalent circuit of an SC. Electrical model.
Charging and discharging of SC at constant current and constant power.
SC Banks: Series, parallel, and mixed association.
Sizing of an SC bank for a specific application. Required capacity. Maximum, minimum, and average voltage (stand-by).
Accumulator parameters: voltage, current, charge capacity, electrical capacity, stored energy, efficiency, self-discharge, discharge constant, and memory effect.
Battery charging and discharging: chargers and regulators.
Production, transport, and storage of hydrogen.
Basic structure of the fuel cell.
Environmental advantages of hydrogen over hydrocarbons.

assessment_methods.method: Two written partial exams (theoretical short answer questions)
Two written partial exams (practical short answer questions)
Active participation in the development of the course through attendance at laboratory practices and individual work for each of them

assessment_rules: For ordinary examination, two partial written exams contribute 45% each to the final grade. Each exam consists of theoretical short answer questions (40%) and practical short answer questions (5%). Active participation and individual lab work account for 10% of the final grade. To pass, students must pass all three parts (two partial exams and participation/work) independently. If any written exam is failed, only the pending part can be retaken in the final exam. For extraordinary examination and differentiated evaluation, a single written exam with theoretical and practical short answer questions accounts for 100% of the final grade.
institution: Universidad de Oviedo - Grado en Ingeniería Eléctrica (EPI Gijón)
